literal: Speaking so that complex matters become easy to understand and penetrate the listener's mind, and oneself discerning the subtle meaning from the mouth of others, is wisdom.
translation: Wisdom is speaking so clearly that complex ideas easily penetrate the minds of others, while being able to discern the subtle, deep truths in whatever others say.
modern: தான் சொல்லும் கருத்துக்களைக் கேட்பவர் மனதில் எளிதாகப் பதியுமாறு விளக்கிச் சொல்வதும், பிறர் பேசும்போது அவர்களுடைய சொற்களிலிருந்து நுட்பமான உண்மைகளைக் கண்டறிந்து கொள்வதும் அறிவாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the two-way nature of wise communication. First, when speaking, a wise person simplifies complex ideas so that they easily enter and settle in the listener's mind. Second, when listening, even if others speak vaguely or poorly, a wise person possesses the sharp intellect to extract the deep, subtle truth hidden in their words. Thus, true wisdom lies in making oneself easily understood while effortlessly understanding the deeper meaning of others.
